task_instance: Perform a monthly bank reconciliation for a sample operating cash account: given a GL cash ledger (9 transactions, Aug 2026) and a bank statement (8 transactions, same period), identify outstanding checks, deposits in transit, and unrecorded bank fees/interest; produce the standard adjusted-balance reconciliation format; build a reconciling-items aging register with category/status/action per the skill's aging buckets; and apply the skill's dollar/age escalation thresholds.
evidence: Created gl_cash_ledger.csv (9 txns, computed ending balance $52,340.00 from a $50,000 opening) and bank_statement.csv (8 txns, computed ending balance $51,340.00) in the work directory. Wrote reconcile.py, which matches transactions by reference, classifies GL-only items as outstanding checks / deposits in transit (Timing Difference) and bank-only items as unrecorded fees/interest (Adjustment Required), computes adjusted bank balance ($52,310.00) and adjusted GL balance ($52,310.00), ages every item against a fixed 'today' (2026-09-27) using the skill's 0-30/31-60/61-90/90+ buckets, and applies the skill's escalation thresholds (>$10k item, >$50k item, >$100k total, >60/90 day age). Ran `python3 reconcile.py` in the work directory; it printed the full reconciliation and an assertion `PASS: reconciliation ties out to $0.00`, confirming the difference between adjusted bank and adjusted GL balances is exactly $0.00. Outputs produced and verified: reconciliation_report.md (full standard-format reconciliation + reconciling items register + escalation analysis + sign-off block with the skill's required financial-advice disclaimer) and reconciling_items.csv (5-row aging register: 2 outstanding checks, 1 deposit in transit, 1 unrecorded bank fee, 1 unrecorded interest credit, all in the 0-30 day 'Current' bucket, none triggering escalation). No external tools, credentials, or network access were needed; the entire deliverable (a reconciliation workpaper) was produced and mathematically verified locally with shell/Python only.
